note: Grassé 1937 described this species as Termes minutus from lowland forest near Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire. The present text adds only soldier measurements and the variation in antennal segment number and contains no complete morphological description; the morphological details still rest on Grassé 1937 and 1944 and on Grassé et Noirot 1951. The original gives the measurements with a comma as the decimal separator, converted here to a point.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: According to Grassé 1937 the soldier antenna usually has 15 segments, but segment 4 may divide again; the present study examined 6 soldiers supplied by Noirot from Côte d'Ivoire, 2 with 14, 2 with 15 and 2 with 16 antennal segments. This variation contrasts exactly with P. mwekerae, in which all 67 soldiers examined have 15 antennal segments; even if the difference were of species-level value, it would be hard to use for identification in a small sample. In this species the widest part of the postmentum is usually nearer the middle of that sclerite, unlike P. hirticeps and P. mwekerae. The soldier likewise secretes a white fluid when disturbed. The nest has been described and figured by Grassé (1937, 1944) and Grassé et Noirot (1951).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Soldier measurements (9 individuals from 2 localities, range/mean, mm): head length (to the outer mandibular base) 1.17—1.31/1.24; greatest head width 0.95—1.06/1.00; head depth (including the postmentum) 0.75—0.80/0.77; postmentum length 0.76—0.86/0.82; greatest postmentum width 0.49—0.55/0.52; least postmentum width 0.46—0.54/0.51; left mandible length 0.60—0.69/0.63; hind tibia length 0.93—1.06/1.00; greatest pronotum length 0.45—0.51/0.49; pronotum width 0.68—0.78/0.73; mesonotum width 0.62—0.70/0.66; metanotum width 0.72—0.83/0.78.
